questions.q: The frequency&  \left(ν\right)$ of an oscillating liquid drop may depend upon radius  \left(r\right)$~of the drop, density  \left(ρ\right)$~of liquid and the surface tension  \left(s\right)$ of the liquid as:~$ν = r^{a}{ρ}^{b}s^{c}$.~The values of $a, b$~and $c$ respectively are&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here, we have& $ν = r^{a}{ρ}^{b}s^{c}$

Equating the dimensions of each quantity on both sides

\left[T^{- 1}\right] = \left[L^{1}\right]a\left[M^{1}L^{- 3}\right]b\left[\dfrac{MLT^{- 2}}{L}\right]c ⇒ T^{- 1} = M^{b + c}L^{a - 3b}T^{- 2c}$

Comparing the dimensions, we get

$c = \dfrac{1}{2}, b = - \dfrac{1}{2}, a - 3b = 0$

$⇒ a + \dfrac{3}{2} = 0 ⇒ a = - \dfrac{3}{2}$

Thus, the value of $a$, $b$ and $c$ are~ \left(- \dfrac{3}{2}, - \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right).

$

questions.q: If mass is written as $m = kc^{P}G^{- 1 / 2}h^{1 / 2}$, then the value of $P$ will be : (Constants have their usual meaning with $k$ a dimensionless constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$m = kc^{P}G^{- 1 / 2}h^{1 / 2}$

Writing dimensions on both sides, we get

\left[M^{1}L^{0}T^{0}\right] = \left[{LT}^{- 1}\right]P\left[M^{- 1}L^{3}T^{- 2}\right]- 1 / 2\left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 1}\right]1 / 2$

By comparing exponent of $L$ on both the sides, we get

$0 = P - \dfrac{3}{2} + 1 ⇒ P = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$

questions.solution: $Let [Y] = [V] ^{a}[\mathrm{~F}]^{\mathrm{b}}[\mathrm{A}]^{\mathrm{c}}\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-1}\right]^{\mathrm{a}}\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]^{\mathrm{b}}\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-2}\right]^{\mathrm{c}}\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrmM^{b} \mathrm{~L}^{\mathrm{a}+b+\mathrm{c}} \mathrmT^{-\mathrm{a}-2 \mathrm{~b}-2 \mathrm{c}}\right]$ Comparing power both side of similar terms we get, $b=1, a+b+c=-1,-a-2 b-2 c=-2$ solving above equations we get $a=-4, b=1, c=2$ so $[\mathrm{Y}]=  \left[\mathrmV^{-4} \mathrm{FA}^{2}\right]=\left[\mathrmV^{-4} \mathrm{~A}^{2} \mathrm{~F}\right]$

Electric displacement

$\overset{→}{D} = {ϵ}_{0}\overset{→}{E}$

\left[D\right] = \left[{ϵ}_{0}$E\right] = \left[{ϵ}_{0}\dfrac{σ}{ϵ0}\right]

\left[$D\right] = \left[\sigma\right]$

questions.q:
In the equation& \left[X + \dfrac{a}{Y2}\right] [ Y - b ] = RT, X$~is~pressure, $Y$~is volume, $R$ is universal gas constant and~$T$ is temperature. The physical quantity equivalent~to the ratio~$\dfrac{a}{b}$ \text{ and } is:

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$X \text{ and } \dfrac{a}{Y2}$~have the same dimensions.~$Y \text{ and } b$~also have the same dimensions.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{a}{Y2} = ML^{- 1}T^{- 2} ⇒ a = ML^{- 1}T^{- 2} \times L^{6} = ML^{5}T^{- 2}$

and~$b = L^{3}$.

So, the dimensions of~$\dfrac{a}{b}$~is,

$\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{ML^{5}T^{- 2}}{L3} = ML^{2}T^{- 2}$.

This is the dimensional form of energy. Hence, this is the right option.

questions.q: Consider the efficiency of Carnot's engine is given by $η = \dfrac{\alpha\beta}{sin\theta}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\dfrac{\betax}{kT}$, where $\alpha$~and $\beta$ are constants. If $T$ is temperature, $k$ is Boltzman constant, $\theta$ is angular displacement and $x$ has the dimensions of length. Then, choose the incorrect option.
options: Dimensions of $\beta$ is same as that of force.
Dimensions of ${α}^{- 1}x$ is same as that of energy.
Dimensions of ${η}^{- 1}sin\theta$ is same as that of $\alpha\beta$
Dimensions of $\alpha$ is same as that of $\beta$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that,& $η = \dfrac{\alpha\beta}{sin\theta}log \left(\dfrac{\betax}{kT}\right).~Since expression inside the logarithm is dimensionless

\left[\betax\right] = \left[$kT\right]$

Since the dimensions of~$kT$~are equivalent to that of energy,

\left[\beta\right] = \left[$kT\right]\left[x\right] = \left[E\right] \left[x\right] = \left[{ML}^{2}$T^{- 2}\$right]\left[$L\right] = \left[{MLT}^{- 2}\right]

Therefore,~\beta~has dimensions of force.

Since~efficiency is a dimensionless ratio,

\left[\alpha\right]\left[\beta\right] = \left[M^{0}L^{0}T^{0}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\beta\right] =1 \left[\alpha\right]

Therefore, dimensions of~\alpha~is not same as that of~\beta.Hence option D is incorrect statement and the answer.

\left[$x\$right]\left[\alpha\right] =\left[\beta\right]\left[$x\right] = \left[{ML}^{2}$T^{- 2}\right]$. Therefore,~${α}^{- 1}x& has dimensions of energy.

$

As we know, angular momentum is given by,& $\overset{→}{L} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{p} ⇒ \left[L\right] = \left[$M^{0}L^{1}T^{0}\right]\left[M^{1}L^{1}T^{- 1}\right]$

Pressure Gradient~$= $\dfrac{dP}{dx}~

Therefore, [Pressure Gradient]$= \left[{ML}^{- 2}T^{- 2}\right]$

questions.q:
Assertion A: Product of Pressure \left(P\right)$~and time \left(t\right)$ has the same dimension as that of coefficient of viscosity.

Reason: Coefficient of viscosity $= \dfrac{Force}{Velocitygradient}$
options: Both A& and R& true, and R& is correct explanation of A.
Both A& and R& are true but R& is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R& is false.
A is false but R& is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Viscous force is given by& $F = ηA \left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right), here,~$A$~is area and~\dfrac{d v}{d t}~is velocity gradient.

Thus,~$η = $\dfrac{F}{A\left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right)}.

Now, $Pt = $\dfrac{F}{A}$t = η \left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right)t$

Then,~\left[Pt\right] = ML^{- 1}T^{- 1} = \left[η\right]

Thus, assertion is true but reason is false.

$
